subject: Re: Draft Order Form - pricing schedule & net terms
messages:
From: Natalie Ruiz <natalie.ruiz@acmeanalytics.com>

Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0500
Subject: Draft Order Form: commercial terms for Redwood deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about moving forward. Attached is our updated draft of the order form (ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3.docx) with a couple of commercial asks we need your help to confirm before we route to procurement:

- Pricing schedule: We proposed a 36-month tiered schedule that steps down at 12 and 24 months. Can you confirm Redwood’s ability to honor the schedule and whether you prefer annual invoicing or quarterly?
- Minimum commitment: ACME is asking for a one-time minimum commit of $450k over 36 months with true-up at year-ends. We currently see different language in the MSA.
- Net terms: they are requesting Net 45 for enterprise customers; finance flagged that as outside your standard Net 30.
- Taxes: they want Redwood to bear VAT for EU-based subsidiaries.

I added inline comments in the Word doc and exported a redline PDF (ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3_REDLINE.pdf) for convenience. Can you introduce us to whoever will handle commercial redlines? Ideally we can have a short call tomorrow to resolve the net terms and invoicing cadence so procurement can get rolling.

Thanks —
Natalie
Natalie Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
Phone: +1 (212) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Draft Order Form: commercial terms for Redwood deployment

Hi Natalie — thanks for sending. Looping in Laura (legal) and Rishi (finance) to confirm on the commercial points below.

High-level responses:
- Pricing schedule: We can accept a tiered structure but need to confirm the exact USD per-unit figures and how usage overage is billed. Laura — any concerns with the stepped pricing from a contract perspective?
- Minimum commit: We typically support minimums; $450k over 36 months is within band but we need to decide whether that is measured as pre-tax or post-tax ARR/usage. Rishi — can finance model the implications if ACME prefers annual invoicing with a year-end true-up?
- Net terms: Our standard is Net 30. We have flexibility to offer Net 45 at the enterprise level for a modest commercial concession or via payment milestones tied to committed spend. Laura — will need to confirm on invoicing language.
- Taxes: We do not typically absorb VAT; we can provide a gross-up in the order form or show tax as a separate line item. Laura, is there any compliance/legal exposure if Redwood explicitly agrees to bear VAT in EU?

Natalie — can you do 30 minutes tomorrow at 11am ET for a quick sync? If not, propose a slot and we’ll work around it.

Regards,
Karthik
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. I reviewed ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3 and the redlines. Quick notes from legal (high level):

- Pricing schedule: legal OK with stepped pricing as long as the order form includes an explicit definition for "Billing Unit" and an authoritative calculation example. We should add a worked example for the first 12 months to avoid disputes on step application.
- Minimum commit: we can accept $450k measured as "Committed Spend" (pre-tax). Suggest adding an annual true-up clause: if actuals < committed, ACME pays shortfall within 45 days of year-end; if actuals > committed, usage billed at standard rates and credited against future invoices. We should be explicit about proration for partial-year terminations.
- Net terms: legal is comfortable with Net 45 as a concession only if the deal gets approved by Finance and Sales; need to add late payment interest at 1.5% monthly and a payment milestone tied to delivery on first invoice to reduce DSO risk.
- Taxes/VAT: Redwood cannot voluntarily assume VAT liabilities for a third party without a signed indemnity and tax covenant. Proposed approach: show VAT as separate line item and add a clause where Redwood will assist with tax documentation; if ACME insists Redwood be the collector, we require tax counsel sign-off and country-specific language.

I drafted suggested language (see attachment: ACME_Redwood_OrderForm_v3_REDLINE.pdf). Rishi — please confirm whether Finance can tolerate Net 45 with a first-invoice milestone and shortfall collection terms. If finance is ok, we can provide a redline to ACME reflecting Net 45 and the other cleanups.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Hi team — quick finance take after running a model on the $450k over 36 months ask:

- If invoiced annually (single invoice per year), cash flow is favorable for ACME but increases our exposure; would prefer quarterly or monthly invoicing with annual true-up. Quarterly invoicing with a payment milestone on first invoice (30% of year-1 commit) is an acceptable compromise.
- Net terms: Finance can approve Net 45 only if we get: (1) a first-invoice upfront milestone of 30% of the year-1 committed amount, (2) an irrevocable PO or equivalent from ACME, and (3) a late fee of 1.5% monthly after 30 days.
- Taxes: We cannot absorb EU VAT. If ACME requires Redwood to act as the VAT payer in-market, they must provide proof of registration/authorization for tax reclaim or, alternatively, agree to a gross-up provision.

Proposed commercial summary to send to ACME (for your review before we redline):
1) Commit: $450,000 over 36 months, measured as Committed Spend (pre-tax).
2) Billing cadence: Quarterly invoices with annual true-up; first-year first-quarter invoice contains 30% milestone of year-1 committed amount due on receipt.
3) Net terms: Net 45 on invoices; late payment interest 1.5%/month after 30 days.
4) Pricing: Tiered schedule as proposed; attach a worked-example appendix.
5) Taxes: VAT shown as separate line; gross-up if Redwood required to collect/absorb taxes.

If everyone is aligned, I can prepare a short redline to the order form and we can circulate to Natalie for signature.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Finance Operations — Redwood Inference
